July 2010 # Choppy copper in the face of financial headwinds - Expectations for consumption are that Q3 will see the recovery continue. Semi fabricators are also facing a tight scrap market, with scrap traders unwilling to release material bought when prices were higher, thus forcing scrap consumers into the cathode market to make up the difference. - Producers are delivering according to plans, but this is not enough to meet increasing demand. This led to a deficit in Q2 and consumers sourcing material from exchange warehouses. Exchange stocks have fallen to below 670,000t at the time of writing. - Prices have been fluctuating in a $6,000-7,000/t range since mid-May, mainly reacting to economic events. The continued recovery in copper consumption will limit the downside, whereas the tightness of the refined market should provide support. |The supply/demand

As in previous months, copper prices have been reactin

g more to macroeconomic events than to current copper market fundamentals. In early June, a weaker euro and signs of a slowdown in the pace of Chinese economic growth put downward pressure on copper prices. In addition, poor US May employment figures in June undermined sentiment about the US economy recovery. These events pushed 3-month LME copper prices on 7th June down to $6,050/t, their lowest trading level since October 2009. However, news about the Chinese government’s decision to allow greater flexibility in the RMB by loosening the peg to the US dollar boosted 3- month prices to over $6,700/t on 21st June from around $6,400/t on the previous trading day. ### **Copper demand continues to see signs of recovery…** While copper prices have been on a downward trend, so have exchange stocks, with the drawdown in stocks reflecting the continued recovery in copper demand as output of semi fabricated copper products shows signs of recovery across all regions. Global production of copper & copper alloy semi fabricated products rose by 10-12% y-o-y in Q1 2010 to almost 5.9Mt. This is the actual consumption of refined copper and high grade scrap. Although this growth rate looks promising, it is a comparison to the worst quarter in 2009. Semis producers report that their order books are being filled for the coming weeks and are expecting the recovery to continue in Q3. However, expectations for Q4 are uncertain as end-use consumers remain cautious. Global consumption of copper and copper alloy mill products (brass mills) recovered by 26% y-o-y in Q1 2010. The improvements in the copper and copper alloy flat rolled product markets are sound, with Asia and the Americas leading with y-o-y growth of 30-40% in the first quarter. Participants in the alloy rod market reported that growth in Q2 remained strong and are feeling more optimistic for Q3. Copper tube remained the weakest link, as world consumption only edged up by 4% y-o-y in Q1, dragged down by negative growth in the Americas. In addition, copper wirerod production increased by 8% y-oy in Q1 to 3.3Mt. North East Asia was the leading growth region rising by 12% y-o-y, followed by the rest of the world (10% y-o-y), North America (4% y-o-y) and Europe (1% y-o-y). US copper wirerod production

Global demand for semi fabricated products continues to increase and is supporting refined consumption by fabricators.  In addition, in the northern hemisphere semis fabricators are restocking ahead of the summer shutdowns.  For example, 3 rod mills in North America are due to close for care and maintenance in Q3:  Nexans in Canada, and Amrod and Southwire in the US.  This is a seasonal pattern, which is reinforced this year by expectations of a good third quarter. 

Japanese semis production is growing more than we had expected, in part due to higher export demand for semis.  Therefore, the domestic market is consuming more refined copper and leading to lower tonnages of cathode available for export.  This will put pressure on the markets that they supply, mainly China.  In fact, Pan Pacific Copper expects Japan to export 8.5% less refined copper, from 590,000t to 540,000t, this year than previously forecasted. 

In addition to increased underlying demand for copper, scrap availability has recently become tighter. We understand that scrap traders that had bought material when copper prices were around $7,000/t are reluctant to sell their inventories at current lower copper prices.  Given the copper price volatility and traders’ expectations that prices will rise in the short term, consumers are struggling to find the scrap they need.  This behaviour is not new; traders will usually hold inventories instead of realising a loss.  Scrap traders do not hedge and mostly deal in cash.  As well as holding material back, availability of scrap is also being constrained by the lower levels of scrap generation due to the slow recovery from the economic crisis in North America and Europe. 

This tightness in the scrap market has materialised despite the fact that Chinese buyers are not as active in the market as they had been earlier this year.  The SHFE/LME arbitrage has been open since mid-May encouraging copper cathode imports and easing the need to import scrap.  Meanwhile, it seems that the implementation of new Chinese regulations to import scrap has gone smoothly and trade has not been significantly affected.  However, consumers in the US report that much of what little scrap is available is being exported to China, leaving a hole in semi fabricators’ requirements in the US market.  In fact, there are indications that #1Scrap in the US is being traded at almost the Comex cash price.  In Europe, Indian buyers of scrap appear to have been more active in the market over the past month.  We think that this is in response to the closure of the two main Indian copper smelters which had closed for care and maintenance.  With less domestic copper available some consumers were looking to source high grade scrap. 

This tightness in scrap availability is, therefore, forcing semis fabricators who normally take scrap to source cathode. 

### **… w

hile copper supply is delivering according to plans, which is not enough…** 

Copper production at mines, smelters, and refineries is performing very well and production targets are broadly being met.  No major disruptions were reported in the first half of the year throughout the copper production chain: mines, smelters and refineries; with refined production estimated to growth at 3.3% y- o-y in Q2.  However, those production targets have fallen short of demand requirements, with the market in Q2 having been in deficit by around 140,000t of refined copper.  It is also interesting to note that there have not been any Chilean cathode tenders since April, an indication that the producers do not have spare material over and above their contracted deliveries.  While we do not expect any in the coming months, any disruption in copper supply will only put more pressure on the refined market. 

### **…and premiums are increasing** 

The necessity of copper consumers to source more material has been rapidly pushing up cathode premiums across regions. The largest increase in copper cathode premiums was in the US, from 4.0-5.0 ¢/lb in May to 5.5-6.5¢/lb in June for delivery on the east coast.  We understand that the main reasons

driving these premiums are higher freight rates (mainly due to transportation companies having gone bankrupt), but also to scrap consumers buying cathode.  However, little new domestic business seems to be coming through, as US consumers are unwilling to pay these high premiums.  In Europe, cathode premiums over the LME cash price have been reported to be up from $60-80/t to $80-100/t.  However, copper consumers said that most deals were agreed at around $90/t. 

The continuous robust growth of copper semis production in China (around 20% y-o-y in the year to May) has increased the needs of material for immediate delivery in China, resulting in copper premiums rising by $20-50/t during the last month, to $100-130/t. 

The fact that premiums are rising across all regions is further evidence that the rise in cathode demand and run down of exchange stocks are mostly due to increased consumption. 

### **At the limit, we are consuming exchange stocks** 

Demand growth outpacing that of supply is leading to a drawdown in exchange inventories.  Several market participants (miners, semis fabricators and traders) confirmed that most of this material (60-80%) is being consumed, although there is also a small element of stocks moving off warrant into cheaper warehouses.  Copper inventories at exchange warehouses (LME, Comex and Shanghai) have declined to their lowest levels since Q4 2009.  At the end of June, overall exchange stocks were slightly below 670,000t, which is an 8% decline m-o-m and 15% below the peak level of 794,000t in February this year. In June, the largest decline was seen at Shanghai warehouses where stocks f

ell by 34,000t of refined copper, a 21% drop m-o-m. Inventories in Comex remain unchanged from May levels and US LME stocks were down by only 3%. ### **Fundamentals to support prices around the $6,500/t level in the near term** Our expectation for the short run is that copper prices will remain sensitive to economic events and fluctuate in a $6,000-7,000/t range. On the one hand, we expect the copper market to move into a surplus in Q3. Copper demand will be at seasonally low levels due to the holiday season (summer months in the northern hemisphere are the quietest of the year). Copper supply, as mentioned above, is performing well and we do not expect major disruptions at mines, smelters or refineries, such that they should deliver near to their annual plans. As a result, we expect a surplus market in Q3 to keep copper prices from not sustainably surpassing $7,000/t. As for investors’ Long positions sentiment, Comex long positions have been liquidated retreat on Comex while short positions remain broadly unchanged, resulting in the net open interest approaching zero. World Adjusted production includes the disruption allowance and the adjustment for raw material availability © 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 7 of 12 Copper Monitor July 2010 www.crumonitor.com # Consumption trends ## **Chinese end use sectors point to sustained semis growth** The rate of increase in Chinese copper consumption is slowing but remains at a high level and we expect refined consumption to grow by 11% in 2010 as a whole. Growth is being driven by developments in several end use sectors, with motor vehicle production the most spectacular. From a low in January 2009, motor vehicle production has risen steadily over the past year to over 16M units, making China the world’s largest vehicle producer. The y-o-y increase peaked at over 140% in January. This is translating into increased demand for copper semis by the industry and will be a support going forward, as vehicle assembly is forecast to slow but not go into reverse. Another important support for sustained copper consumption growth in China is the extension of the scrappage scheme for domestic appliances to the end of 2011. Appliance production (the sum of washing machines, refrigerators and freezers) has been boosted remarkably by the scrappage scheme, as the chart on the right indicates. Production returned to trend last year and has leapt well above it in the March-May period in 2010, with an annual increase of over 33% y-o-y in the first five months of 2010. Both of these end use sectors represent the rise of the Chinese consumer as a source of domestic demand for copper containing products. With the need to rebalance the economy away from exports, the rise in consumer demand will be a key support for copper consumption going forward, along with the sustained need for copper intensive infrastructure investment. ## **Wire and cable recovery on track** At CRU’s 4th World Wire and Cable Conference in Gothenburg, Sweden the recovery in demand Sustained recovery in Chinese

The severity of the recession means that if there was no upturn the market would be in a deep depression! Of course, the conference speakers and participants confirmed that the recession was most pronounced in the developed markets of North America and Western Europe, where the shape of the upturn is looking like an “extended U”, rather than © 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 8 of 12 Copper Monitor July 2010 www.crumonitor.com the V seen elsewhere. This is reflected in the share value of the wire and cable industry tracked by CRU, which had quadrupled from 2003 through 2007 but the increase was completely wiped in the subsequent 18 months. Wirerod production to feed wire and cable production in North America and Western Europe combined fell by 7% in 2007 and a further 19% last year. In Q1 2010, we estimate that production grew by only 4% y-o-y in these two regions combined. The cable industry continues to shift to the new “new world” of countries such as Vietnam, China, India, Latin America and North Africa at the expense of the “old world” of North America and Western Europe. Presenters and delegates from these growth markets were very bullish on selected regional and country growth opportunities. This is supported by our reading of production of copper wirerod in the world excluding North America and Western Europe, which fell by just 2% last year and has risen by 9% y-o-y in Q1 2010. Mergers and acquisitions (M&A) are on the increase, with telecoms having supplanted the financial sector as the lead sector for activity. In the first five months of this year telecoms M&A has already achieved 2/3 of the deal volume seen last year and is on course to be the year with the second highest ever deal volume. In the wire and cable industry (and the whole of the copper semis industry as well), those players who are cash positive may be in a position to pick assets from their less fortunate competitors. The option for Enami to sell the 10% stake in the copper deposit would be one of the measures to finance reconstruction after the earthquake in Chile.  The possible transaction is valued at US$50M by industry sources. Quebrada Blanca is expected to produce 84,000t of SXEW copper cathode in 2010. 

- On 3<sup>rd</sup> June, the Zambian government announced that it is planning to build a new power plant as a joint venture between **Lunsemfwa Hydro Power Company** and **InfraCo** , a European-funded infrastructure project developer in sub-Saharan Africa.  The project would add 120MW power generation capacity to the country.  Lunsemfwa said that the feasibility studies will start in July and be concluded in June 2011.  The construction of the project is scheduled for May 2012 to April 2016 and is estimated to cost between US$220M and US$275M.  Mines in Zambia suspended output on 18<sup>th</sup> June after a power blackout. **Konkola Copper Mines** said that production resumed on 19<sup>th</sup> June and **First Quantum Minerals** said that the **Kansanshi** mine resumed full production after losing 9 hours of power.  It is reported that **Lumwana** mine and the **Bwana Mkubwa** plant have also resumed production. 

- **Xstrata** has suspended a A$600M (US$488M) project to extend the life of the **Ernest Henry** copper mine.  This involves the loss of 60 contractor jobs with immediate effect and 190 positions that would have be created in the next 18 months for the project.  The decision follows Xstrata’s review of investment in its Australian operations and projects as a result of the Australian Government’s proposed Resource Super Profits Tax.  The Ernest Henry underground mine project was approved by Xstrata in December 2009 and would have extended the life of the EHM operations from 2013 to at least 2024.  EHM’s current open pit mining operations would have been progressively transformed into a major underground mine through the investment. CRU expects Ernest Henry to produce 91,000t of copper-in-concentrate in 2010. 

- On 7<sup>th</sup> June, **Capstone Mining Corp.** said it will suspend mining and milling operations at its **Minto** mine for 5-7 days due to a spreading wildfire.  As a result, the company reduced its workforce to a maintenance crew.  The wildfire spread along the west bank of the Yukon River and reached 6km from the mine.  The company later announced that Yukon Wildland Fire Management successfully completed the burn out around the southern and eastern perimeters of the mine, which reduced the risk of the fire spreading into the mine area.  Capstone said that full operations resumed on 14<sup>th</sup> June.  We estimate that the Minto mine produced 25,000t of copper concentrate in 2009 and will produce 24,000t of copper concentrate in 2010. 

## **Exploration and Development** 





- On 31<sup>st</sup> May, **Antofagasta Minerals** said that the **Esperanza** copper-gold projec

t in northern Chile will use a 145km pipeline to pump sea water from the shore to the project’s grinding and flotation plant.  The US$2.3B project involves a capacity of 95,000t/d for which 650l/s of sea water will be needed.  Esperanza is anticipated to start operation by October 2010 with production expected to reach 700,000t/y of concentrates containing 195,000t of copper. 

- **Lumina Copper Chile** , owned by **Pan Pacific Copper** , on 2<sup>nd</sup> June submitted a request to national water authority DGA for the approval of a freshwater pumping system for its **Caserones** copper-molybdenum project in northern region III.  The complete pipeline will be 89.6km and will provide freshwater to the project’s processing plant.  Caserones started its construction phase in April 2010 and is expected to produce its first cathode and copper-in-concentrate in 2013.

- **Copper Mountain Mining Corp** said on 31<sup>st</sup> May that it has signed US$322M in debt financing agreements for the development of its **Copper Mountain** project in southern British Columbia.  Financing was arranged by Mitsubishi Materials Corp and consists of US$162M provided by a consortium made up of **Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi UFJ Ltd** and **Mizuho Corporate Bank** , and a term loan of US$160M from **Japan Bank for International Cooperation** .  We expect full production to begin in June 2011. 

- In early June, **Codelco** said that it would start operations of a project to process sulphide copper ore from its **Radomiro Tomic** mine in the second week of the month.  The US$370M project aims at processing 100,000t/d of sulphide ore from Radomiro Tomic at **Chuquicamata’s** concentrator plant, with ore being transported via a 9km conveyor belt from the mine.  CRU expects the Radomiro Tomic mine will produce 38,000t of copper-in-concentrate in addition to 297,000t of EW cathode this year. 

- On 1<sup>st</sup> June, **Minera Quadra** submitted an EIS to local environmental regulator Conama for its **Sierra Gorda** copper-molybdenum project in northern region II.  The project consists of an open pit mine, an SX-EW operation and a concentrator plant to process 190,000t/d of oxide and sulphide copper ore and produce 138,000t/y of copper, including copper-in-concentrate and cathodes.  However, days later the project hit a setback due to the collapse of a proposed joint venture between China’s **State Grid International Development** ( **SGID** ) and Minera Quadra’s parent company, **Quadra FNX Mining** , in which Quadra would contribute Sierra Gorda and its Franke mine, and SGID was to take a 50% stake. The JV was intended to raise capital to finance Sierra Gorda’s construction. 

- On 9<sup>th</sup> June, the legislative council of the Philippine province of South Cotabato approved the open pit ban under the province's Environment Code, in response to re

sidents’ concerns about pollution of a major river used to irrigate farms.  The ban was originally proposed in 2005.  The decision will become law within 30 days from 9<sup>th</sup> June if there is no move from the provincial governor.  This ruling affects the **Tampakan** copper-gold project, co-owned by **Xstrata** and **Indophil Resources** , which aims to start production in 2016. **Indophil** suspended its shares after reports of the proposed mining ban, and a takeover bid of the company by China’s **Zijin Mining** was terminated due to “uncertainties”. Indophil’s 37.5% stake in Tampakan is now up for sale. The project has an estimated resource of 2.2Bt containing 12.8Mt of copper. 

- On 9<sup>th</sup> June, **Grupo Mexico** said that it began repairing damage at the **Cananea** copper pit after a police raid ended a three-year-long strike on 6<sup>th</sup> June.  Unionised miners were forced to leave the installations by federal police.  The company estimates that it will cost approximately US$100M to repair Cananea. 

## **Smelting and Refining** 







- In late May, it was reported that **Sumitomo Metal Mining** may maintain production cuts of 10% in the year from 1<sup>st</sup> April 2011, as a result of lower processing fees and a well-supplied domestic market.  In 2010, Sumitomo is expected to produce 405,000t of copper cathode. 

- Zambia's **Chambishi** copper smelter has begun negotiations with mining companies for copper concentrates aimed at expanding its processing capacity to 250,000 t/y of blister copper from the current 150,000 t/y.  Earlier this year the company announced a second phase of the US$130M smelter expansion. The project will be delayed if favourable commercial terms were not agreed.  The smelter is owned by two Chinese state companies: **China Nonferrous Metal Mining Group** (60%) and the **Yunnan Copper Industry Group** (40%).  All the feedstock for the smelter is currently bought from the domestic market, with **Equinox Minerals’ Lumwana** mine a major supplier. 

- Members of the United Steelworkers Canada union ratified a tentative deal with **Xstrata Copper Canada** for a new 3-year collective bargaining agreement at the company's **Montreal** refinery.  The tentative

**Yunnan Copper Corporation** announced on 30<sup>th</sup> June that it will reduce operations in its **Kunming** plant in order to conduct planned checking and maintenance on the number 2 furnace smelting system, the ISA furnace and the ISA waste heat boiler between 1<sup>st</sup> July 2010 and 1<sup>st</sup> April 2011. Yunnan reports that although refined copper production and sulphuric acid production at this plant will be affected, the company will still be able to meet its 2010 production target o

f 320,000t of refined copper by refining more blister and anode copper in order to offset reduced copper concentrate smelting activities. 

## **Consumption** 









- **Hitachi Cable Ltd** . plans to invest ¥3-4B (US$33-44M) building an industrial cable plant at a site in the northern Vietnamese province of Hai Duong, which could be in production as early as fiscal 2012, exporting to Southeast Asia, China and Japan.  The company is positioning this site as its core base in the Southeast Asian region. A 10,000m<sup>2</sup> plant to produce wiring for equipment is already under construction. 

- China’s **Golden Dragon Holding Co Ltd** says it has recently shut down its phase 2 copper tube project in Mexico. This follows the US Commerce Department’s decision to impose preliminary anti-dumping duties on imports of certain seamless refined copper pipe and tube from both China and Mexico (at margins ranging from 10.26 to 60.50% and 29.52 to 32.27% respectively). The GD group’s current annual production capacity is 220,000t, including 150,000t of grooved tubes. 

- China’s **Ministry of Finance** said in a statement on 22<sup>nd</sup> June that export tax rebates on certain copper, zinc, lead, nickel and tin products such as tubes and wires will be removed from 15<sup>th</sup> July. The tariff change, which will reduce exporters’ margins and could affect refined consumption, follows increasing trade complaints from the U.S. and the European Union. 

- French cablemaker **Nexans** said it plans to use 25,000t of recycled copper to produce cables in 2010, compared to 9,000t in 2009.  Nexans has recently opened a cable recycling plant, **Recycable** , with **Sita France** near its Lens facility.  The plant has a capacity of 35,000t/y and will increase to 50,000t by 2011.
